statement: Organise user-defined properties into named groups, each property having a unique name within its group, a description and a data type, available to elements and to building materials.
superiority: Groups can be defined by rule or schema file and diffed in version control.
notes: CORRECTED — groups hold properties and availability is set by classification; IFC mapping is a separate translator preset. Read Property Manager. Acceptance sketch: Create group with 3 properties, assign to Walls: all walls expose the 3 fields, values persist after save.

statement: Define typed properties as string, number, integer, length, area, volume, angle, true/false, option set or tags list, with a description, so entered values must match the type.
superiority: Strict typed schema with units checked end to end, including Python API.
notes: CORRECTED — types listed are string, number, integer, length, area, angle, volume, tags list, option set, true/false; no date type documented. Read Property Manager. Acceptance sketch: Entering text into an integer property is refused; a length property converts when the project length unit changes.

statement: Offer option-set properties with a fixed list of labelled options and an allow-multiple-choices switch that lets one element hold several of them.
superiority: Options can be linked to external dictionaries (bSDD).
notes: VERIFIED — read Property Manager; option sets cannot be expression-defined, multi-choice ones cannot be used inside expressions. Acceptance sketch: Selecting 2 options of 3 stores both; schedule shows list.

statement: Give each property a default that is undefined, a fixed value or an expression, with element values staying linked to the default until a custom value is entered, so editing the default updates every linked element.
superiority: Defaults documented per tool in the schema.
notes: CORRECTED — defaults are linked, not copied at creation; unlinking and relinking via chain icon documented. Read Default Property Value, Assign Custom Property Value. Acceptance sketch: Editing a property default updates all elements still linked to it and leaves elements with a custom value unchanged.

statement: Control per property or group whether it is available to all, no or custom classifications, with branch selection in the classification tree and an apply-to-sub-items action.

source.ref: Property Manager > Property Availability for Classifications

superiority: Availability rules support nested conditions and queries.
notes: CORRECTED — availability is by classification (all/none/custom), not directly by tool type. Read Property Availability for Classifications. Acceptance sketch: Property shows only on walls classified as external wall.

statement: Map Archicad properties and parameters to IFC properties in translator presets for export, and on import either keep IFC properties as read-only IFC properties or map them onto existing Archicad properties through a mapping table.

source.ref: IFC > Property Mapping for IFC Export / Import

superiority: Mapping is two-way and checked by round trip tests.
notes: CORRECTED — export mapping tree per IFC entity plus import mapping table documented; no new properties are generated on import. Read Property Mapping for IFC Export, Property Mapping for IFC Import. Acceptance sketch: Exported file contains Pset with value; import recreates the property.

statement: Show and edit the classification and property values of the selected elements in a classifications-and-properties panel of settings dialogs and the info box, with a search field to find a property.

source.ref: User Interface Reference > Classifications and Properties Panel

superiority: Palette searchable with filters and pinned groups.
notes: CORRECTED — no dockable 'properties palette' found; the panel lives in settings dialogs and the info box. Mixed-value display not confirmed in help. Read Classifications and Properties Panel. Acceptance sketch: Selecting two walls and editing a property in the panel writes the value to both; typing in the search field filters the listed properties.

statement: Expose geometry and model data of each element type, such as dimensions, areas, volumes, elevations, layer and building materials, as built-in listing parameters usable in schedules, labels and criteria.
superiority: Every geometric value is exposed and traceable to its formula.
notes: CORRECTED — built-ins are called listing parameters, organised per element type, plus properties. Read Element Listing Parameters, Property Manager (built-in and custom properties). Acceptance sketch: Wall volume property equals geometric volume to 1e-9.

statement: Give elements a free-form ID that auto-increments any number inside it for each newly placed element, alongside a permanent unique identifier, without automatic prevention of duplicate IDs.
superiority: Stable GUID plus human-readable ID.
notes: CORRECTED — no uniqueness check or 'position number' is documented; duplicates after paste are left to the user. Read ID Management, Classifications and Properties Panel. Acceptance sketch: Placing three walls with ID W-1 yields W-1, W-2, W-3; duplicating a wall keeps its ID.

statement: Give each element a renovation status of existing, new or to be demolished, settable from a palette or the settings panel with a default for new elements, which renovation filters use to show, hide or override it.

source.ref: Renovation > Assign Renovation Status to Elements

superiority: Phases drive a version diff report.
notes: VERIFIED — read Assign Renovation Status to Elements and Renovation Filters; default status is existing. Acceptance sketch: Elements with status New display under the New Construction renovation filter only.

statement: Let an element be marked load-bearing or non-load-bearing as its structural function, and interior or exterior as its position, used for core-of-load-bearing display, find and select, and the IFC load-bearing and external flags.
superiority: Directly feeds analysis model.
notes: CORRECTED — structural function and position are two-valued settings, not a position-number property. Read Classifications and Properties Panel, Assign or Edit IFC Property/Attribute Values. Acceptance sketch: Property exports as IFC LoadBearing.

statement: Support user-defined rating properties, such as fire resistance as an option set, that are scheduled, mapped to IFC and usable in graphic overrides.
superiority: Code compliance checks run on properties.
notes: CORRECTED — help gives Fire Resistance Rating as a user-created property example, not a built-in compliance property. Read Properties and Classification Systems, Property Manager. Acceptance sketch: Rating text appears in schedule.

statement: Let expression properties read an element's surroundings, such as the related zone number or zone data, so the link between an element and its zone is derived rather than stored.
superiority: Containment is computed live.
notes: CORRECTED — expressions can draw on model environment such as the surrounding zone; a 'reference level' property is not documented. Read Expression-Defined Element Properties, CONCAT example. Acceptance sketch: A door's derived zone-number property changes when the zone number changes, with no manual edit.

statement: Provide net, gross and conditional volumes and projected areas of components, with openings subtracted, ignored, or ignored by project calculation rules, for quantity take-off.
superiority: Net and gross logic exposed as explicit parameters.
notes: CORRECTED — net/gross/conditional variants exist for component volume and projected area. Read Component Listing Parameters in the Interactive Schedule. Acceptance sketch: Net area equals gross area minus openings to 1e-9.

statement: Provide the exposed area of each surface, discounting parts covered by other elements, so finish quantities per surface or material can be listed.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Exposed Area parameter in Surface Schedules

superiority: Face-level quantity by orientation.
notes: CORRECTED — exposed area with user-defined covering elements replaces a plain per-material area. Read Surface Schedules, Exposed Area parameter in Surface Schedules. Acceptance sketch: The sum of per-material areas equals the total surface area.

statement: Export a project's properties, with group, type, default value, availability and option sets, to an XML or project file and import them into another project.

source.ref: Property Manager > Export/Import Properties Between Projects

superiority: Open JSON schema with diff.
notes: VERIFIED — read Export/Import Properties Between Projects; classifications can be included on request. Acceptance sketch: Export then import into an empty project reproduces every group and property.

statement: On importing properties that already exist, append the duplicates with a suffix, and on importing classification systems merge them with a dialog for handling duplicate classifications.

source.ref: Property Manager > Export/Import Properties Between Projects

superiority: Three-way merge with explicit choice.
notes: CORRECTED — conflicts are handled by Append (suffix) for properties and Merge for classification systems. Read Export/Import Properties Between Projects. Acceptance sketch: Importing a property whose name exists appends a suffixed copy and keeps both; merging a system adds only classifications not present.

statement: Hold project info as predefined and user-defined fields in reorderable groups, usable in autotext, expression properties, IFC properties and BIMx output, with export and import.
superiority: Project data reachable from scripts.
notes: VERIFIED — read Project Info and Using Project Info throughout your project; version 30 added custom groups and fields. Acceptance sketch: Project name in title block updates.

statement: Offer library part parameters as criteria and fields in schedule schemes beside properties, found by folder, name search or favorites.

source.ref: Interactive Schedule > Additional Criteria and Fields: Library Part Parameters

superiority: Parameter names are unified with property names.
notes: CORRECTED — parameters are offered in schedule criteria and fields; labels and generic properties are not documented. Read Additional Criteria and Fields: Library Part Parameters. Acceptance sketch: A library part parameter chosen as a field appears as a schedule column with each placed object's value.

statement: Create and manage classification systems and hierarchical classifications with ID, name and optional description, duplicate them, and import or export them as XML or project files.
superiority: Supports live bSDD dictionaries.
notes: VERIFIED — read Classification Manager; named standards such as Uniclass not verified in help so removed. Acceptance sketch: Import tree of 1,000 items; hierarchy preserved.

statement: Assign an element or building material to a classification in each loaded system at once, through a classification-and-properties panel, with the classification deciding which properties it receives.
superiority: Rule-based assignment by query.
notes: CORRECTED — assignment is through the settings panel, not a separate palette. Read Assign Classification. Acceptance sketch: Element has two systems assigned; both exported.

statement: Let tool favorites store classification and property values so newly placed elements start with them.
superiority: Defaults come from the template.
notes: CORRECTED — Favorites explicitly store Classification and Properties data; tool default dialogs carry the same panel. Read Favorites, Classifications and Properties Panel. Acceptance sketch: A favorite saved with classification Wall-External places new walls carrying that classification.

statement: On IFC import, map imported IFC types, with predefined and user-defined types, to classifications of a chosen target classification system.

source.ref: IFC > Type Mapping for IFC Import

superiority: Maps to standard dictionaries.
notes: CORRECTED — import creates classification assignments through type mapping into an existing system rather than creating classification items. Read Type Mapping for IFC Import. Acceptance sketch: Classification preserved after import.

statement: Export assigned classifications as IFC classification references when the export data conversion preset includes classifications.

source.ref: IFC > Data Conversion for IFC Export

superiority: Checked against the schema in CI.
notes: VERIFIED — read Data Conversion for IFC Export; manual references also in Create New Classification Reference. Acceptance sketch: The IFC contains an association entity per classified element.

statement: Link classification items to buildingSMART Data Dictionary entries.
superiority: Offline cache of dictionaries.
notes: REJECTED: no buildingSMART Data Dictionary integration in Archicad 30 help; searched bSDD, data dictionary and classification pages (Classification Manager has no such link). Acceptance sketch: Looking up an item returns the dictionary name and URI.

statement: Let find-and-select and schedule criteria test classification (is, is not, under or directly under a classification within a system) and whether a property is defined or undefined.

source.ref: Property Availability for Classifications (Find and Select)

superiority: Combined with property criteria.
notes: CORRECTED — documented tests are IS / IS NOT, IS UNDER / IS DIRECTLY UNDER, and defined/undefined. Read Property Availability for Classifications, Define Element Criteria. Acceptance sketch: A filter returns exactly the classified elements.

statement: When importing a classification system that already exists, merge it so classifications not yet present are added and duplicates are resolved through a dialog.

source.ref: Property Manager > Export/Import Properties Between Projects

superiority: Version diff with mapping of changed IDs.
notes: CORRECTED — merge with duplicate-handling dialog documented; no id-mapping of renamed items found. Read Export/Import Properties Between Projects, Classification Manager. Acceptance sketch: Merge-importing a newer system adds its new classifications, keeps existing ones, and asks what to do for each duplicate.

statement: Allow expression properties to use arithmetic operators and comparisons over unit-typed values, with the result type checked against the property's data type.
superiority: Expression language typed and testable with unit checks.
notes: VERIFIED — read OPERATORS (+ - * / ^ = <> < <= > >=) and Errors in Expressions and How to Fix Them. Acceptance sketch: Expression width*height gives area in m2 for 1.2x2.1.

statement: Provide text functions in expressions such as CONCAT, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, FIND, REPLACE, SUBSTITUTE, SPLIT, TRIM, UPPER and LOWER.

source.ref: Functions in Expressions > TEXT EDITING FUNCTIONS

superiority: Full function table documented.
notes: VERIFIED — read TEXT EDITING FUNCTIONS and CONTAINS; list includes CONCAT, LEFT, RIGHT, MID, REPLACE, UPPER. Acceptance sketch: Concat of prefix and ID produces expected string.

statement: Provide the logical functions IF, IFS, AND, OR, NOT, XOR and ISUNDEFINED with comparison operators, plus CONTAINS as a text-search test.
superiority: Same rule engine as graphic overrides.
notes: CORRECTED — CONTAINS is a string function, not a list test; IFS, XOR, ISUNDEFINED added. Read LOGICAL FUNCTIONS, CONTAINS. Acceptance sketch: IF(h>3,"tall","low") correct for both cases.

statement: Provide statistical and math functions such as SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, ABS, ROUND, ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN, MROUND, MROUNDUP, MROUNDDOWN, POWER, SQRT and MOD, requiring identical data types and compatible units across arguments.
superiority: Aggregates over related elements, such as all doors in a zone.
notes: CORRECTED — help has MROUNDUP/MROUNDDOWN rather than CEILING/FLOOR; mixed-type SUM(1, 2m) is an error. Read MATHEMATICAL FUNCTIONS, STATISTICAL FUNCTIONS, All Arguments Must Use the Same Data Type. Acceptance sketch: SUM(1m, 2m) returns 3 m; SUM(1, 2m) is rejected; MROUNDUP(2567, 10) returns 2570.

statement: Let an expression refer to built-in parameters, other custom properties and project info by name, including single-choice option-set properties.
superiority: Dependency graph is shown.
notes: VERIFIED — read Expression-Defined Element Properties and Property Manager; cycle detection is not documented, sketch is a Dino requirement. Acceptance sketch: A property reference resolves and a cyclic reference is detected and refused.

statement: Evaluate expression-defined properties in schedules, labels and zone stamps, but not for properties assigned to building materials.
superiority: Uniform across schedules, labels and filters.
notes: CORRECTED — evaluation sites are schedules, labels, zone stamps; not evaluated for building materials; not in settings dialogs. Read Expression-Defined Element Properties, Evaluate Expression-Defined Property. Acceptance sketch: An expression property appears as a schedule column with the right value.

statement: Let text and autotext labels embed property values as autotext entries beside typed text, and offer labels that list chosen properties of the element they point at, staying associated with the element.
superiority: Typed placeholders with preview.
notes: CORRECTED — property data shown through autotext and property labels; prefix, suffix and unit formatting not documented. Read Text/Autotext Labels, Show Property Data in Labels and Markers. Acceptance sketch: A placeholder prints the value with its unit and prefix.

statement: Provide an expression editor with a function pop-up, hover descriptions with syntax and argument data types, and error messages when the result conflicts with the property's data type.
superiority: Autocomplete and live evaluation.
notes: VERIFIED — read Using Expression Editor and Errors in Expressions; preview with sample values is not documented, element evaluation is. Acceptance sketch: Syntax error is reported with position.

statement: Let expressions compute zone-based quantities, such as a window glazing ratio against the zone's net area, to show regulation compliance per element.
superiority: Domain function library for rooms.
notes: CORRECTED — help gives zone-ratio compliance example (Example 7) and area-division example. Read Example 7: Display Regulation-Compliance Data for an Element, Divide [/]. Acceptance sketch: A finish area expression equals perimeter times height minus openings.

statement: Allow properties and classifications to be assigned to building materials as well as to elements, with expression-defined values evaluated for elements only.
superiority: Dino can evaluate expressions on materials too, giving schedules per-material computed data.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Properties and Classification Systems and Expression-Defined Element Properties; materials take properties, expressions are not evaluated for them. Acceptance sketch: A property assigned to a building material is editable in the material's settings and appears in a material schedule.

statement: Import a buildingSMART information delivery specification file to generate the classifications and properties it requires, adding only new items into a chosen IFC property mapping preset and reporting results in a session report.

source.ref: Interoperability > Import Properties and Classifications with IDS

superiority: Dino can also validate the model against an IDS file and report failing elements, not just import definitions.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Import Properties and Classifications with IDS; import only adds, never modifies existing items. Acceptance sketch: Importing an IDS file listing 5 properties of which 2 exist adds 3 and leaves the 2 unchanged; the next IFC export carries all 5.

statement: When hotlinked modules carry properties or classifications absent from the host, show them read-only and greyed, searchable and schedulable, with a per-row merge into the host and an option to list those that differ.

source.ref: Property Manager > Properties and Classifications in Hotlinks

superiority: Dino can reconcile module and host definitions automatically by a stable property identity instead of names.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Properties and Classifications in Hotlinks; values map by property name and become undefined if types are incompatible. Acceptance sketch: A module property missing in the host is listed greyed, appears as a schedule field with the module's values, and becomes editable after merge.

statement: Check an expression property's result type against its declared data type and its function arguments for identical types and compatible units, reporting a specific error such as type conflict, wrong argument type or mathematical error.

source.ref: Property Manager > Errors in Expressions and How to Fix Them

superiority: Dino can underline the failing argument inline and offer an automatic unit-correct rewrite.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Errors in Expressions and How to Fix Them and All Arguments Must Use the Same Data Type and Compatible Units. Acceptance sketch: SUM(1, 2m) is reported as an argument type error and SUM(1m, 2m) is accepted for a length property.

statement: Let the user evaluate an expression-defined property for the selected elements, from the property manager and from a calculator control in the info box property list.
superiority: Dino can show evaluation of every intermediate step so the user sees why a value is what it is.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Evaluate Expression-Defined Property; a new property must be saved before it can be evaluated. Acceptance sketch: Selecting an element and evaluating a width times height property shows the product in the element's unit.

statement: Convert unit-typed values to text in the project's calculation units and text to numbers inside expressions, so descriptive strings can combine measured values with unit tags.
superiority: Dino can offer unit-aware text formatting with explicit locale and unit arguments.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read DATA CONVERSION, Convert Unit to String [STRCALCUNIT] and Contains [CONTAINS]; STR, STRCALCUNIT and STRTONUM exist. Acceptance sketch: Converting a 25 mm length with calculation unit millimetres gives the text 25; STRTONUM of a numeric string multiplied by 1 cm returns a length.

statement: Maintain a keynote database as a hierarchy of folders and keynotes with key, title, description and reference, import or export it as XML or XLSX with merge or replace, and place keynotes through labels and autotext.
superiority: Dino can link keynotes to classification items so notes follow the element's classification automatically.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Keynotes and Import/Export Keynotes; merge conflict handling is skip, overwrite or append. Acceptance sketch: Exporting the keynote database to XLSX and importing it with replace reproduces every key, title, description, reference and folder path.

statement: Place a keynote legend on a layout that lists all keynotes or only those visible on the drawings, with chosen fields per column, optional folder rows and a display option for conflicting hotlink data.
superiority: Dino can generate the legend as a live schedule with the same formatting engine as other schedules.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Keynote Legend and Legend content and format; legend is an object-type element with filter, field, merge and format pages. Acceptance sketch: A legend filtered to visible keynotes lists exactly the keynotes used by labels in the placed drawings.

statement: Let a library part maker define listing properties for a new library part from a default scheme, a custom scheme object, or an Excel sheet with group, name and typed values, exposed as non-editable parameters for schedules.

source.ref: Library Part Maker > Import Property Data from Excel

superiority: Dino can bind listing properties straight to the same property system used for elements, with no separate scheme object.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Customizing Data Properties, Create Custom Property Scheme and Import Property Data from Excel. Acceptance sketch: Importing a sheet with 3 typed columns yields a part with 3 non-editable listing parameters of the given types.

statement: Provide an element ID manager that renumbers elements of a chosen type, optionally only the selection, by sorted criteria and a four-part ID format combining text, counters and story number, with saved settings.
superiority: Dino can renumber incrementally and stably so existing IDs never change unless the user asks.
notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Element ID Manager and ID Management; floor plan only, Sort Elements and ID Format tabs. Acceptance sketch: Renumbering 10 doors grouped by story with format D-<story>-<counter> yields D-1-01 to D-1-05 and D-2-01 to D-2-05.
